hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Uneven Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: Significant cracking and displacement of sidewalk slabs create tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Vegetation Encroachment
hazards.description: Grass and weeds growing through cracks and from the edges reduce the usable width of the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk on the left side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the roadway shoulder near apartment buildings.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway adjacent to the white fence and apartment building.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian refuge areas visible, forcing pedestrians to cross an wide, unmarked expanse of road.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire width of the road

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible, making it difficult for pedestrians to safely cross the wide residential street.

hazards.name: Lack of street lighting
hazards.description: No street light poles are visible, which may create safety and security concerns for pedestrians at night.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway with no planting strip or parked cars to separate pedestrians from moving traffic.

hazards.name: Potential for high vehicle speeds
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway geometry without traffic calming encourages higher speeds in a residential area.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The roadway is wide with no mid-block crossing or refuge, requiring pedestrians to cross multiple lanes and parking zones unprotected.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side of the image is cracked and overgrown with vegetation, creating a tripping hazard.

hazards.name: Uneven and cracked sidewalk
hazards.description: The concrete sidewalk shows significant cracking and vertical displacement, creating a tripping hazard for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, along the bottom edge of the properties

hazards.name: Wide straight roadway
hazards.description: The wide, straight geometry of the road encourages higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicle
hazards.description: A large white van parked at the curb obstructs the sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, parked along the curb.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from vegetation
hazards.description: A large tree near the sidewalk edge can partially block the view of pedestrians for oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, between the sidewalk and the road.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane without a buffer or parked cars to protect pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Uneven walking surface
hazards.description: Concrete sidewalk slabs show signs of displacement and vegetation growth in joints, creating potential trip hazards.

hazards.name: Long unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a refuge island or marked crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: The existing sidewalk on the far side is directly adjacent to the curb with no physical separation from moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk on right side
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a dedicated pedestrian walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk in an undefined parking area or the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Driveway
hazards.description: The sidewalk effectively disappears into a large paved lot for vehicle access, creating a conflict zone where pedestrians have no defined or protected path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, spanning the frontage of the auto shop

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is positioned in the center of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the clear walking width.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: The wide, straight travel lanes and shoulders lack physical constraints, which typically encourages higher vehicle speeds in residential areas.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: Multiple driveway curb cuts along the left sidewalk create frequent points where turning vehicles may cross the pedestrian path.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: In a residential area with houses on both sides, the absence of a marked crossing point increases risk for pedestrians crossing mid-block.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge island, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Walkway Obstruction
hazards.description: A large box truck and an SUV are parked directly on the paved area intended for pedestrians, blocking the path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground on the paved apron.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The parked box truck creates a significant blind spot, preventing pedestrians and drivers from seeing each other at a conflict point.

hazards.name: Undefined Conflict Zone
hazards.description: The lack of clear separation between the roadway, parking area, and pedestrian walkway creates confusion and increases the risk of vehicle-pedestrian collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground area between the road and the building.

hazards.name: Continuous Curb Cut
hazards.description: The entire frontage of the commercial property on the left is a flush curb cut, allowing vehicles to enter and exit the parking area at any point across the pedestrian path.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles are parked directly on the paved area intended for pedestrian travel, forcing walkers into the roadway or between parked cars.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side, near the commercial building

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide safe pedestrian separation.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and curb extensions to reduce crossing distances and improve visibility at crossing points.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to physically reduce vehicle speeds to levels appropriate for a residential street.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation or Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the driveway entrance to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Treatment
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk material and level across the driveway to signal pedestrian priority and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with appropriate signage to provide safe and predictable crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions

interventions.title: Speed Humps or Tables
interventions.description: Introduce vertical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds along this residential corridor.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Speed humps or cushions
interventions.description: Install vertical deflection measures to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential zone.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair or replace the damaged concrete sections to provide a continuous, smooth, and accessible walking surface.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Implement a regular maintenance schedule to clear weeds and grass from the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion

interventions.title: Mid-block Pedestrian Crossing

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing/Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Reduce the effective width of the travel lanes through striping or curb extensions to encourage lower vehicle speeds in this residential zone.

interventions.title: Speed Humps

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to encourage slower vehicle speeds in this residential area.

interventions.title: Install Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale lighting to improve visibility and safety for people walking after dark.

interventions.title: Add a Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a vegetated buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to increase the physical and psychological distance between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Implement Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Install speed humps or other measures to ensure low vehicle speeds on this residential street.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve safety and visibility during night hours.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Completion

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair or replace the cracked and uneven sections of the sidewalk to provide a smooth, accessible walking surface.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Speed Cushions
interventions.description: Implement speed cushions to reduce vehicle speeds to levels appropriate for a residential street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Mark a high-visibility crosswalk to designate a safe crossing location for pedestrians in this residential area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer/Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair and level uneven sidewalk slabs to improve accessibility and reduce trip hazards.

interventions.title: Street Trees

interventions.title: Install Sidewalk on Near Side

interventions.title: Sidewalk Resurfacing

interventions.title: Speed Cushions or Humps

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
